messages:
maya_s: Heads-up — product asked if we can expose per-tenant SLO visibility + an override flow in the Console. They want a way to mark certain tenants as 'strict' so alerts for them never get auto-suppressed.
chris_t: Can you paste the ask? is this about notify suppression or threshold edits?
dana: It’s both. They want two things: (1) dashboard badge + filter for strict tenants, (2) an override toggle so Ops alerts always fan out for that tenant even during global quiet windows.
pm_rachel: Correct. Enterprise customers with compliance needs need guaranteed notifications. They still want noise controls but an explicit override for specific SLOs/tenants is required.
eli: Quick concern: if we allow per-tenant force-fanout, we might amplify alert storms and hit paging limits. Need rate limits + opt-in confirmation.
chris_t: Agreed. Proposal: implement a tenant-level "notify_policy" enum: OFF/DEFAULT/FORCE. FORCE always bypasses suppression filters but still respects per-recipient rate limits.
maya_s: How would this look in Console? My mock: small lock icon + tooltip on tenant header, and a confirm modal when you flip to FORCE explaining cost and on-call impact.
dana: UX should also surface which SLOs are covered by the toggle (e.g., critical vs non-critical). We shouldn't implicitly override low-priority alarms.
eli: Implementation note: back-end needs to tag routed alerts with tenant.notify_policy and short-circuit suppression stage. Also add a feature flag so we can rollout gradually.
chris_t: Pseudocode for routing stage:

```
if tenant.notify_policy == "FORCE":
  bypass_suppression = true
else:
  bypass_suppression = evaluate_suppression_policies(req)
```

We still run fanout with normal retries and recipient quotas.
pm_rachel: Product asks for audit trail — every time FORCE causes an alert to go out it should create an 'override' audit entry visible in the tenant timeline.
maya_s: Ops-bot can log the audit entry via an event sink. ops-bot: created ticket infra-ops/alert-override-logging to track schema.
ops-bot: Note: infra-ops/alert-override-logging created by maya_s.
dana: For SLO configuration, owners should be able to opt individual SLOs into FORCE rather than whole-tenant too. Example: tenant A forces critical SLOs only.
eli: That complicates the data model but is doable: keep notify_policy on both tenant and slo objects; slo-level policy overrides tenant-level when present.
chris_t: We need guardrails: UI warns "SLO-level FORCE will override tenant-level suppression and may generate pages for responders not on the SLO rotation."
pm_rachel: Also request: expose metrics in the Console: count of FORCE-bypassed alerts per-week and estimated paging cost.
maya_s: Action items: (1) chris + eli prototype backend toggle + flag, (2) dana + maya mock UX + confirmation modal, (3) pm_rachel to draft audit/event schema, (4) add metric in telemetry team backlog.
chris_t: I'll open an RFC in docs repo with the routing code changes and a proposed DB migration. Target: canary behind feature flag in 2 weeks.
dana: Will post UX mocks in #design and link here when ready.
eli: One more: ensure we can't FORCE for managed shared routes (hosted shared customers) without legal sign-off. Add a tenancy check at API.
pm_rachel: Noted. Thanks all — this looks actionable.
maya_s: Closing loop — I'll add the modal text draft to the RFC and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
